title: Greatest real root of a biquadratic equation
source: Theory P1-1.5 Quick check 1 (x^4-5x^2+4=0, greatest root 2); book Worked example 1.10 style p.15, new numbers
stem: Solve \(x^4-({S|int})x^2+{P|int}=0\). What is the greatest real root?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Let \(u=x^2\). Then \(u^2-{S|int}u+{P|int}=0\), so \(u=( {a|int} )^2\) or \(u=( {b|int} )^2\). Hence \(x=\pm {a|int}\) or \(x=\pm {b|int}\). The greatest real root is \({a|int}\).
steps.note: The quadratic in u has roots a^2 and b^2. Space the braces so that {a|int} is not adjacent to a TeX brace. a>b>0.

title: Smaller positive root of a biquadratic equation
source: Theory P1-1.5 Quick check 2 (same family, smaller positive root 1); book style p.15, new numbers
stem: Solve \(x^4-({S|int})x^2+{P|int}=0\). What is the smaller of the two positive roots?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Let \(u=x^2\). Then \(u^2-{S|int}u+{P|int}=0\), so \(x=\pm {a|int}\) or \(x=\pm {b|int}\). The two positive roots are \({a|int}\) and \({b|int}\). The smaller is \({b|int}\).
steps.note: Same substitution as Quick check 1. a>b>0.

title: Greater solution of a quadratic in 2^x
source: Theory P1-1.5 Quick check 3 (2^{2x}-6*2^x+8=0, greater x=2); book Worked example 1.12 style p.16, new numbers
stem: Solve \(2^{2x}-({S|int})\times 2^x+{P|int}=0\). What is the greater of the two real values of \(x\)?

steps.name: A
steps.text_tex: Let \(u=2^x\). Then \(u^2-{S|int}u+{P|int}=0\), so \(u=2^{ {p|int} }\) or \(u=2^{ {q|int} }\). Hence \(x={p|int}\) or \(x={q|int}\). The greater value is \({p|int}\).
steps.note: The roots for u are 2^p and 2^q. Spaced braces avoid adjacent {{ from TeX. 2^x is one-to-one, so the x-values are p and q.

contexts.note: Includes the original p=2, q=1, greater=2
